raw.assessment: The incumbent achieves intended coverage in 32/40 exports (80%), below 95%, with median handling of 17 rather than at most 12 minutes. Assignment changes and renames accompany all eight affected exports, suggesting unstable course interpretation without proving causation. The seven-minute median for unchanged-assignment centers limits any universal bottleneck account: routine exports can already require little handling. Replacement delivery greatly exceeds execution time, but waiting and active handling are distinct. Zero cross-center rows supports only the sampled cases; the split-course center was excluded.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments may exclude courses intended for a historical week; renames may instead produce apparent omissions during name comparison.
openings.delta: Separate actual membership errors from label mismatches before choosing a correction.
openings.prediction: With weekly membership fixed independently, assignment changes alter exported membership if temporal selection is responsible; renames preserve membership but alter coordinator judgments if labels are responsible.
openings.probe: Compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, and renamed courses in private staging, varying assignment and name separately. Obtain agreed expected membership and coordinator judgments. Preserve the documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry; share a six-day total budget with Z2 within existing hosting.
assumptions: Expected membership can be agreed independently of current labels.
Historical assignment availability and production correction feasibility remain unproven.

openings.claim: Does replacement handling mainly involve requesting and tracking delivery, or checking and spreadsheet work after delivery?
openings.delta: Identify active work separately from elapsed waiting before changing replacement access.
openings.prediction: Immediate availability reduces active minutes if delivery coordination dominates; comparable active effort persists if checking or importing dominates.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators' two short sessions with comparable fabricated CSV tasks. Counterbalance ordinary request handling and immediate availability; separately time requesting, checking, correction, download, and import. Retain private, center-scoped access, schema compatibility, concurrent attendance entry, and the shared budget.
assumptions: Shorter delivery delay alone establishes neither lower handling time nor better coverage.

raw.assessment: Two existing by-products offer testable reuse opportunities. Their existence is stipulated; their adequacy and causal contribution remain unproven. Neither opening alone establishes the 40-export success targets.

openings.claim: Can existing center schedules, including weekly handwritten annotations, supply enough dated evidence to reconstruct intended course membership for a requested week?
openings.delta: Reuse coordinator-maintained scheduling traces as a temporal test oracle for fabricated staging exports, turning after-download comparison into evidence for diagnosing selection errors.
openings.prediction: If these traces retain usable history, coordinators can independently distinguish a rename, an instructor reassignment, and a course split for the same requested week. If they contain only current names, this reuse fails.
openings.probe: In consenting coordinators’ sessions, inspect relevant traces inside authorized workspaces and record their source and update time. Ask coordinators to reconstruct dated course sets before seeing exports. Translate supported cases into fabricated staging fixtures and compare outputs; mark disagreements or missing history unresolved.
assumptions: Historical details are not established by the mere existence of schedules.
The bounded diagnostic exercise fits six engineer-days and existing staging capacity.
Attendance entry continues; the documented CSV remains supported.

openings.claim: An existing job-completion trace might also serve as a private replacement-file readiness signal, reducing coordinator waiting when a usable replacement is already available.
openings.delta: Give the completion trace a delivery-coordination role beyond recording execution and row totals.
openings.prediction: This helps only when completion-to-retrieval accounts for substantial delay; request-to-start delays or course-selection defects would remain.
openings.probe: For consented replacement requests, collect request, job-start, completion, and retrieval times within authorized workspaces. Verify whether completion can be securely associated with the correct center, requested week, and ready file. Trial a workspace readiness cue using fabricated data only if that association exists.
assumptions: Completion logs are supplied; request timestamps, artifact links, and center identifiers are not confirmed.
A readiness cue must not imply course-set correctness.
Proceed only if implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting without blocking attendance entry or changing the CSV schema.

openings.claim: Historical assignment selection may omit courses; renames may cause apparent omissions.
openings.discriminator: Membership changes versus changed coordinator judgments with membership fixed.
openings.probe: Vary assignment and name independently in fabricated staging against agreed weekly membership.
openings.uncertainty: Correlation is not causation; historical data and correction feasibility unknown.

openings.claim: Immediate replacements may reduce delivery coordination work.
openings.discriminator: Active work falls versus checking/import effort persisting despite shorter waits.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary requests and immediate availability across six coordinators’ two sessions; time requesting, checking, correction, download and import separately.
openings.uncertainty: Fabricated tasks may not transfer; waiting differs from handling.

openings.claim: Schedules and handwritten annotations may reconstruct historical intended membership.
openings.discriminator: Dated traces distinguish reassignment, rename and split versus current names only.
openings.probe: Inspect authorized traces with source/update times; reconstruct before viewing exports; translate supported cases into fabricated fixtures.
openings.uncertainty: History/completeness unknown; park disagreements and missing history as unresolved.

openings.claim: Completion traces may support private replacement readiness cues.
openings.discriminator: Completion-to-retrieval delay versus request-to-start delay or selection defects.
openings.probe: Collect request/start/completion/retrieval times; verify center/week/file association before fabricated cue trial.
openings.uncertainty: Timestamps, identifiers and artifact links unconfirmed; readiness cannot certify coverage.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before implementation. All probes share six engineer-days and existing hosting; preserve private center-scoped processing, documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry. Split-center isolation remains untested. Stipulated synthetic evidence establishes no success: require next-40 median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended coverage and zero cross-center records.
